newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares ease 0.9 pct toward 80,000 support.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares ease 0.9 pct toward 80,000 support.

text.p: Istanbul shares continued to slide in thin volume on Thursday towards support levels after failing to overcome stiff resistance on Monday, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed down 773.70 points, or 0.94 percent at 81,441.31, bringing three-day losses to 3.84 percent since Monday's 1.03 percent rise to an all-time high close of 84,692.20.
Trade volume decreased to 13.29 trillion lira from Wednesday's 14.24 trillion.

"Sales began because the market could not pierce resistance at above the 85,000 mark (on Monday). Reports on expectations that JCR may cut Turkey's credit rating also sparked anxiety and buoyed sales in the afternoon," said Okan Alpay from Interbank.
Turkish bankers and newspapers say Japanese credit rating agency JCR may downgrade Turkey's BB+ rating soon.

Monday's was the third attemt to break the 85,000 barrier. It had drifted lower in a week-long limited pull back after the first attemt on October 31, following a 29.3 percent rally and ten record closes from September 13 to October 23.
"I believe the index will touch 80,000 levels or even 79,000 this time," said Filiz Tiken from Sinai Yatirim Kredi Bank.

Of the 226 shares traded, 110 declined, 50 advanced and 66 were unchanged. The 85-share industrial index eased 0.69 percent to 86,307.91 and the 15-share financial index dropped 1.49 percent to 78,293.15.
Leading actives were utility Aktas Elektrik, steady at 98,000 lira and largely state-owned petroleum refiner Tupras, down 1,500 lira at 20,000. Together, they made up 15 percent of the total volume.
